description.en-US: Two-tier command execution: provably read-only commands run without approval (shell_read, parser proof layer); any other single simple command is allowed into the approval card (shell) — no command-level bans since v2.145 (ZCode alignment)
description.zh-CN: 命令执行两态：可证明只读的命令免审批（shell_read，解析器证明层）；其余任何单条简单命令一律放行进审批卡（shell）——无命令级禁令（v2.145 对齐 ZCode）

tools.description: Run ONE simple command and return {command, program, exit_code, success, timed_out, truncated, stdout, stderr}. Any single simple command is allowed — it will ask the user for approval first (approve once, for this session, or always for this project). No command is banned outright, but prefer `shell_read` for read-only work (no approval needed). Pipes, command substitution and shell metacharacters are rejected — pass a single simple command. Commands run WITHOUT a shell: the first word is spawned directly via PATH. On Windows hosts PATH usually resolves to Unix coreutils (Git's usr/bin) — use Unix-style commands; cmd builtins (dir, del, copy, `rmdir /s /q`) do not exist.
tools.name: shell

command.description: single simple command, e.g. "git status"; no pipes/semicolons/backticks

cwd.description: optional working directory (absolute path, must exist)

max_bytes.description: cap stdout/stderr each (default 65536, env LOCOWRK_SHELL_MAX_BYTES, max 262144)

tools.description: Run ONE PROVEN read-only command WITHOUT user approval: ls, cat, grep, git status/log/diff/show/--version, pwd, node -v/--version, python/python3 --version. A proof layer parses the command (lexing + structure + semantics): it must be a single simple command — no unquoted pipes/redirection/`$()`/backticks/subshells, no `$` or backticks inside double quotes; no git global options (`-c`, `--git-dir`, ... can launch external programs via config); no write or external-program flags (`--output`, `--ext-diff`, `--textconv`); no credential paths (.env, .ssh, credentials, key material). Anything that cannot be PROVEN read-only is refused: re-run via the `shell` tool (asks the user) or pass a simpler command. Same result shape as `shell`. Paths must stay inside the allowed file roots (LOCOWRK_FS_ROOTS, default = app data root) — this includes the optional cwd argument; anything resolving outside is refused. Commands run WITHOUT a shell: the first word is spawned directly via PATH. On Windows hosts PATH usually resolves to Unix coreutils (Git's usr/bin) — use Unix-style commands; cmd builtins (dir, del, copy, `rmdir /s /q`) do not exist.
tools.name: shell_read
